identity_check: Confirmed as Hadrian (Hadrian Automation, hadrian.co), the advanced-manufacturing company founded in 2020 by Chris Power that builds highly automated factories making precision parts for aerospace and defence; its releases are datelined Torrance, California, and every round page (company blog, PR Newswire, TechCrunch) describes the same company and CEO. Not FBR's 'Hadrian X' bricklaying robot or any other company using the Hadrian name. Category kept adjacent (PROJECT_CONTEXT §7 had remote): Hadrian is mainly a vertically integrated parts manufacturer, but it now also sells its Opus factory-autonomy software inside customer plants (a seven-year deal to run cells in Lockheed Martin's Grand Prairie site), says Opus interprets legacy designs, and runs Atlas, a vetted-supplier and DFM program, which touches Utopian's drawing / procurement functions. It does not sell agents to plant staff or work over WhatsApp, and serves US defence primes rather than Indian factories. Layer full_stack_factory.

company.name: Hadrian
company.description: Torrance, California manufacturer running highly automated, software-driven factories that make precision parts and assemblies for aerospace and defence.

layer_detail: Owner-operator of automated machining, inspection and additive factories (two in Torrance CA, Mesa AZ, Cherokee AL) run on its Opus factory-autonomy software; also deploys manufacturing cells inside customer plants and runs Atlas, a vetted-supplier + DFM program for hardware startups
named_customers: U.S. Navy (Columbia- and Virginia-class submarine programs)
product_summary: Makes precision components, assemblies and finished products for aerospace, defence and space in highly automated factories run on its Opus AI platform, which reads legacy designs and automates machining and inspection. Also sells dedicated factory capacity or cells inside customer plants, and Atlas, a vetted-supplier and DFM program.

open_items: Jan 2026 T. Rowe Price-led 'expanded capital': amount and series not disclosed; the release gives only the $1.6B valuation (recorded as post-money, not stated which).
Series D release says the financing 'will be co-led' by the named firms and does not say whether the round has closed.
Series B leads not named; TechCrunch also mentions 'around $25 million in debt financing for equipment and expansion' and it is unclear whether that is inside the $117M equity-and-debt figure.

Debt not recorded as rounds: Morgan Stanley factory-expansion loan facility with the Series C (amount not stated) and a $360M revolving credit facility closed 2026-08-14 (Morgan Stanley Senior Funding lead left arranger).

Factory 4 (Cherokee, Alabama, Mar 2026) is a public-private partnership with >$1.5B of Hadrian private capital and $900M of Navy appropriations; government funding is not a venture round and is not recorded.

Total raised: sum of disclosed equity rounds is $1,846.5M (seed through Series D, Series B includes some debt) plus the undisclosed Jan 2026 round; TechCrunch (Jul 2025) said 'nearly $500 million' raised since 2020, consistent with the $476.5M sum to Series C.
Headcount: only Fortune's Oct 2024 'over 200 full-time employees' found; releases talk of hiring thousands, 350 jobs at Mesa and up to 1,000 at Factory 4, but give no current total.
Revenue not publicly reported on any page read. Fortune (Oct 2024) cited a reported ~$500M valuation not tied to a round; not recorded.
Hadrian acquired Datum Source (Aug 2024, per TechCrunch headline on hadrian.co/press); an acquisition by Hadrian, not a funding round; article not read.
CNBC (2022 and 2025), WSJ and Bloomberg funding coverage returned 403 or were not read; web-search budget was exhausted, so 2026 rounds were found through PR Newswire's Hadrian newsroom listing.
